pollIntervalMs.description: How often a client should re-read the board

ChartSeries.description: Pageviews per bucket from each provider on the union of their axes. A null provider has not seen it; a null value is a bucket it has not reached.

RatedVitalsRow.description: One host's web vitals, rated against Google's Core Web Vitals boundaries (null: not measured).

SectionFailure.description: Sections of one source that could not be read at all, failing with the same error.

SiteReport.description: What one site has, and only that: an absent figure is null or empty. `empty` says nothing has anything to draw.

ErrorsViews.description: What the Errors pages draw from PostHog's per-site sections: the site list, the sites with the most errors, each site's report, and which sections could not be read.

post.summary: Requirement B: write the board into the ledger — opens, updates and resolves rows (can alert)
post.description: Runs the monitor cycle's own ledger write. It opens a row for every derived problem that has none, refreshes the rows of problems still live, and resolves the ones the board no longer derives. Opening a row (and closing one as a recovery) queues an alert, which this endpoint flushes — so calling it can page on-call.

200.description: Counts of what the ledger write did

get.summary: One cursor-paged page of the activity feed, older than the given cursor
get.description: The cursor is the (before, beforeId) PAIR because a deployment's build and deploy rows share a timestamp. Both halves are required together — half a cursor is a client bug, and answering it with the newest page would silently restart the scroll at the top, so a lone half 400s. An empty `beforeId` alongside a `before` is still a valid cursor: it is the pagination stall escape the server itself mints when a full page of events shares one millisecond.

200.description: One page of the activity feed, oldest-first

get.description: Error/fatal log lines and 5xx responses of each production project’s current production deployment, as the monitor cycle last read them. Grouped by project, source, method, normalized path, status and first message line; `count` is lines since `firstSeen` (7-day retention). Worst level first, then most frequent. `total` counts every group in the window; `groups` is capped at 200.

get.summary: One-call health digest of every source: verdict, findings, coverage, sections
get.description: Reads the monitor, deploys, integrations, GlitchTip and PostHog errors, Vercel runtime errors, PostHog and Vercel analytics, and uptime in parallel. Every judgement is the server’s: `verdict` is the worst finding (critical→down, major→degraded, minor→attention; none → healthy when `complete`, else unknown). `complete` is false when any source could not be read, a dashboard section failed or was still refreshing at the `wait` deadline, or the monitor stopped probing; providers with no credentials are listed under `coverage[*].unconfigured` and do not clear it. A section is null exactly when its source could not be read. The MCP tool `get_report` returns the same payload.
